name: The Two Reductions of a Rooted Square Assembly
statement: For a rooted square assembly from nontrivial corner-peelable ample factors $A,B$, marked edge endpoints $a_0,a_1$, and hole $q=(q_e,q_f)\ne00$, its two square-coordinate reductions are the vertex gluings $A\vee_{a_{1-q_f}}B$ and $A\vee_{a_{1-q_e}}B$. Each reduction is corner-peelable exactly when $A$ peels to its indicated attachment vertex. If the assembly is forbidden and that vertex is unattainable, then $A$ rooted there is itself a rooted factor. For the opposite hole $q=11$, the whole assembly equals the coordinate-block replacement of $A\vee_{a_0}B$ and is forbidden exactly when $(A,a_0)$ is a rooted factor; no marked-edge retention conditions are needed.
proof: In either square reduction, a nonroot word of $B$ survives only in the row opposite the corresponding bit of the hole, while the root survives in both rows. This is exactly vertex gluing at the stated endpoint. The vertex-gluing theorem gives the peeling equivalence. A negative reduction of a forbidden assembly descends to a cut-vertex obstruction, forcing the stated rooted factor. For hole 11, the four square rows coincide with the block replacement of the gluing at $a_0$; block replacement and the cut-vertex theorem give the exact forbiddenness criterion.
comments: Adjacent holes attach the second factor to the two different marked endpoints. Unmarked uniqueness of the decomposition is not asserted.
